title: plugin-charts: a line or area chart clips its last x-axis label at the plot's right edge — "2026-10" is drawn as "2026"
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"marchtian"} -->
_Requested by **田騏** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi?thread=cmsg_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi7SkqaNxU2Ef8P2DMmp2hPJ)_

Found during an exploratory walkthrough of the showcase dashboards (objectui `main` @ `6fb31dc`, objectstack `main` @ `b9c7a8f`, 1440×900).

## Where

- Showcase → 数据分析 → 图表画廊 (Chart Gallery): **Tasks Created (monthly)** (line) and **Tasks Created (area)** both show the x axis as `2026-09 … 2026`.
- Showcase → 营收概览（带筛选） (Revenue Pulse): **Invoices by Month** (line) shows `2026-08  2026-09  2026`.

## What is happening

The tick text in the DOM is complete: reading the `.recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value` elements on the Chart Gallery returns `2026-09`, `2026-10`. The last label is centred on the final data point, which sits on the plot's right edge, so its right half falls outside the chart's clip area and only `2026` remains visible.

The bar charts on the same pages do not have the problem (Revenue Pulse **Accounts Signed by Month** shows `2026-08` and `2026-09` in full), because a band axis puts the last category in the middle of its band rather than on the edge.

## Why it matters

The cut label reads as a different, coarser bucket (a year), so the newest month on a trend chart, the one a reader looks at first, is the one that is mislabelled.

## Suggested direction

Give line/area charts a little horizontal padding on a categorical x axis (recharts `padding={{ left, right }}` on `XAxis`), or keep the first and last ticks inside the plot (anchor them `start` / `end`), so edge labels are not clipped.
